explanation: Dried currants are tiny black grapes whose name comes from Corinth in Greece; they are unrelated to blackcurrant bushes. Sultanas are usually pale seedless grapes.

claims.text: Raisins, sultanas and dried currants are all dried grapes.
Raisins, sultanas and dried currants are not made from plums, cherries or figs.
The name currant comes from Corinth, in Greece, through the Old French 'raisins de Corauntz'.
Dried currants come from small black grapes and are not related to blackcurrant or redcurrant bushes.
Sultanas are usually made from pale, seedless grapes.
